Hi Samantha — great question and thanks for the PO. I pulled together the mechanics below and looped in Ben (partner ops) and Lauren (pricing) for any detailed evidence or accounting examples. High level:

- Overage smoothing: by default our private offer bills actual usage each month. For customers with variable spikes we offer an optional smoothing configuration — we call it a rolling 90-day smoothing window. Under that mode, we compute a rolling average of the last 90 days of consumed node-hours and cap invoiced overage charges to at most 1.5x the rolling average in any single invoice cycle. Any excess usage above that cap is carried forward as a usage credit applied to future invoices until consumed. Example: if rolling avg = 100 node-hours and month spike = 280 node-hours, invoiced overage is limited to 150 node-hours and the remaining 130 hours become a deferred credit.

- Why it helps: evens out cashflow and avoids one-off big invoices; preserves unit economics by deferring but not forgiving usage. Credits expire after 12 months if not drawn down.

- Partner brokerage/commission waterfall: partner brokerage is calculated on net invoiced revenue after list-price passbacks and discounts. Order of operations (simplified): list price -> private-offer discount -> regional tax adjustments -> invoiced net -> apply listprice passback (if marketplace sale) -> compute partner brokerage % on resulting net revenue -> partner payout. For overage credits, the partner brokerage is adjusted when the credit is applied (i.e., if an overage is deferred and later credited, partner calculations are reconciled in the next settlement cycle).

I attached a commissioning matrix (v3) that shows sample splits and the reconciliation row for deferred credits. Ben — can you drop a sample invoice snippet and confirm settlement timing? Lauren — anything to add on contract language we should include in the SOW about expiration of credits?

Samantha — looping in operational examples. Attached is a redacted invoice snippet and a 3-row settlement extract. Key points:

- Invoice snippet (line items): base reserved capacity, monthly actual usage, overage adjustment (deferred-credit applied), tax lines, total due. We include a reference to the private offer id so procurement can map charges to the PO.
- Settlement timing: partner brokerage is paid monthly on a 30-day lag after invoice finalization. When a deferred credit reduces prior invoiced revenue, we perform a reconciliation entry in the next settlement month and adjust partner payout accordingly (positive or negative).
- Evidence: we can provide a simulated invoice PDF and the CSV settlement extract for TechDistrib for the first 6 months if that helps procurement/finance validate the cashflow model.

Operational note: if Evergreen requires zero retroactive negative adjustments to partners, we can structure the partner payout to reserve the brokerage amount in a 60-day escrow and release after smoothing window closes — this is doable but will require a short addendum to the partner MSA.
